context:
Goal: builders and reviewers judge screens by one list.
Problem (rule): the house-rules record lists 14 ids, while the design docs hold 34 ux headings, and no check compares them.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/ux-house-rules.md:14-19 lists 14 ids as the house rules.
Based on (read): docs/design/principles.md has 27 ux headings and docs/design/layout.md has 7.
Based on (read): no lint or hook reads either list.
Departs from: main, with two lists that differ — makes one list and checks it.

options.gain: One list; every ux heading binds builders and reviewers.
options.how: The record cites the headings in principles.md and layout.md instead of listing ids. A check fails when a cited heading is missing.
options.label: All 34 are house rules
options.lose: 20 more rules bind every screen review.

options.gain: Fewer binding rules on each screen review.
options.how: Keep the record's list. Mark the other 20 headings as guidance, and add a check that the 14 exist as headings.
options.label: Only the 14
options.lose: Two kinds of ux heading for readers to tell apart.

ref: deep audit 1102, report docs/plans/deep-audit/report.md on audit/deep-1102 (6b6a41f3), table 'claude-settings: homes', row ux-house-rule-ids
title: Are all 34 UX headings house rules, or only the 14 the record lists?
why: Builders already read the design docs whole; one list with a check ends the drift.
